name: Try-Catch Error Handling
description: Wrap external calls and I/O operations in try-catch blocks. Return structured error responses instead of throwing.
when_to_use: API calls, file operations, database queries, external service integrations
example: try { const result = await fetch(url); } catch (error) { return { error: error.message, status: 'failed' }; }

name: Database Singleton Pattern
description: Use a singleton pattern for database connections. Initialize once, reuse everywhere. Close on process exit.
when_to_use: Any application using a database connection
example: let _db: Database | null = null; function getDb() { if (!_db) _db = new Database(path); return _db; }

name: Parameterized SQL Queries
description: Always use parameterized queries (? placeholders) instead of string interpolation for SQL. Prevents SQL injection.
when_to_use: Every SQL query that includes user-provided values

name: Conventional Commits
description: Use conventional commit format: type(scope): description. Types: feat, fix, refactor, docs, chore, test.

name: Python3 Stdin Piping for JSON
description: When parsing JSON in bash scripts, pipe file content via stdin to python3 instead of interpolating paths into python code.
when_to_use: Any bash script that needs to parse JSON files
example: VALUE=$(python3 -c 'import json, sys; data=json.load(sys.stdin); print(data["key"])' < file.json)

name: Idempotent Script Design
description: Scripts should be safe to run multiple times. Use mkdir -p, CREATE IF NOT EXISTS, INSERT OR IGNORE. Check state before acting.
when_to_use: Setup scripts, migration scripts, initialization scripts

name: SQLite WAL Mode for Concurrency
description: Enable WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode for concurrent read access. Set busy_timeout for write serialization.
when_to_use: Any SQLite database that may be accessed by multiple processes
example: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000; PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL;

name: FTS5 Content-Sync Pattern
description: Use FTS5 content= tables with AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers to keep full-text index in sync with main table.
when_to_use: When you need full-text search on SQLite tables
example: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t_fts USING fts5(col1, col2, content=t, content_rowid=id);
